subject: Request: retroactive surge cap & rate upgrade — BrightEdge
messages:
From: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@brightedge.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightedge.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected Nov surge — asking for retro cap and smoothing

Hi Tessa,

We had a substantial, unanticipated surge in usage the weekend of Nov 24 (launch of a new feature) that pushed us well past our committed throughput. Our engineering team attached the usage breakdown (see attached usage_report_nov.pdf) — the overrun looks concentrated in three 6-hour windows.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood make the quota uplift retroactive to Nov 24 so the Nov invoice can be smoothed (we want a single true-up rather than multiple line items)?
- Given this was operational and tied to our launch, is there a one-time concession you can offer on the overrun rate (we were expecting to be able to rely on transient headroom)?

Procurement looped me in (procurement@brightedge.ai) because we may need an amendment/PO for the uplift. We’d like to close this quickly — can you confirm next steps and whether you’ll be able to make any temporary rate adjustments while we sign paperwork?

Thanks,
Sylvia Chen
Head of Platform
BrightEdge

[attachment: usage_report_nov.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@brightedge.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Nov surge — asking for retro cap and smoothing

Sylvia — thanks for the heads up and for the usage file. I’m sorry that launch caused a spike. We can absolutely propose a short-term remediation plan to avoid an awkward invoice for you while paperwork is worked out.

High-level proposal (for quick approval):
- Temporary quota uplift ("Burst-2" throughput tier) applied retroactively to Nov 24–Dec 10 to cover the identified windows.
- Prorated true-up on the Nov invoice that consolidates overrun into one line item.
- One-time concession: a credit applied against the true-up (we can propose a % discount on the overrun volume).

I’m looping Ben and Marcus for pricing/approval and to finalize numbers. If that direction works for BrightEdge, we’ll prepare an amendment (DocuSign) and a short MAP to get the uplift scheduled as soon as procurement signs.

Would you be available for a 20-minute call today to confirm the effective retro date and agree on the credit amount?

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Nov surge — pricing recommendation

Quick pricing recommendation based on the usage report:
- Temporary uplift: Burst-2 tier (adds 3x concurrent QPS headroom) applied retroactively Nov 24–Dec 10.
- Overrun true-up: consolidate all excess usage into the Nov invoice line.
- Concession: 20% discount on overrun volume between 100M–500M tokens; for overs >500M we keep standard overrun rate (to limit exposure).
- One-time credit: $5,000 applied to the invoice to offset launch friction; any credit > $10k requires Finance sign-off (we should escalate if Sylvia asks for more).

I attached a quick worksheet showing the math and projected invoice impact. If Tessa gives word, I’ll flag this to Finance for expedited approval and prepare the DocuSign amendment for a retro effective date.

[attachment: surge_pricing_calc.xlsx (XLSX)]

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@brightedge.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightedge.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Nov surge — pricing recommendation

Tessa / Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround. The outline sounds reasonable. A few clarifying notes from procurement:
- We can accept a retroactive uplift to Nov 24 if it’s documented in an amendment and countersigned.
- The 20% discount on the 100M–500M band is acceptable; can you confirm the resulting invoice total after the $5k credit? procurement needs a single number to approve.
- We will need the amendment routed via DocuSign (procurement prefers that workflow).

If you can send the amendment and the one-line estimated invoice total today, procurement will prioritize the PO. Otherwise we may need a short checklist to ensure our legal team can sign promptly.

— Sylvia
Sylvia Chen
Head of Platform, BrightEdge

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Nov surge — pricing recommendation

Sylvia — appreciate the quick confirmation. Finalizing next steps below so procurement has everything in one place:

1) Scope & dates: Burst-2 uplift retroactive Nov 24, 2026 through Dec 10, 2026. This will cover the three windows in your usage report.
2) Billing impact: We will consolidate excess usage into a single Nov true-up line. After applying the 20% concession on the 100M–500M band and the $5,000 one-time credit, the estimated net increment to the Nov invoice is $27,450 (please treat as provisional until Finance posts the final true-up).
3) Amendment & signatures: I will route an amendment via DocuSign for the retroactive uplift and credit. Link: https://www.docusign.com/brightedge/AMEND-8721
4) MAP & operations: Attached is a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP-8721.pdf) showing the timeline for scheduling the uplift and when billing will reflect the change.
5) Approvals: Ben will seek Finance sign-off early next week (any >$10k credit or deviation is escalated).

Procurement: when you receive the DocuSign, a countersignature will authorize the retroactive uplift and the one-line true-up entry on the Nov invoice. If you prefer a PO instead of DocuSign, reply and we’ll accept a PO number and route the amendment internally.

I’ll follow up Monday to confirm Finance has cleared the credit. Happy to hop on a call if useful.

Thanks,
— Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
